problem: If $U={1,2,3,...,100}$ is the universal set and $S={1,3,5,...,99}$, then $\overset{―}{S}=$
worked_solution:
The complement of $S,$ denoted $\overset{―}{S},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $S.$

The universal set $U$ consists of the integers $1$ through $100,$ while the set $S$ consists of the odd integers $1$ through $99.$

So, the only elements of $U$ that are not in $S$ are the even integers $2$ through $100.$

Therefore, the complement of $S$ is

$$
\overset{―}{S}={2,4,6,...,100}.
$$
